item.title: Tarique returns home after five-day US visit
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman returned home on Sunday morning after wrapping up his five-day visit to the United States to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA).
“An Emirates flight carrying the Prime Minister, his wife Dr Zubaida Rahman and members of his entourage reached Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport via Dubai around 8:21am,” PM’s Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu told UNB.
After a six-hour transit stop in Dubai, the Emirates flight departed Dubai International Airport for Dhaka at 2:15am local time, Shiplu said.
Tarique arrived in Dubai from New York at 8:23pm local time on Saturday on an Emirates flight after leaving New York on Friday night.
At John F Kennedy International Airport, Tarique and Zubaida were seen off by Bangladesh Ambassador to the United States Tareq Md Ariful Islam, Bangladesh’s Permanent Representative to the UN Irene Khan and senior officials of the UN mission and embassy.
The Prime Minister arrived in New York on September 21 to attend the UNGA and delivered his maiden address as Prime Minister at the General Debate on September 24.
During the five-day visit, he held around 30 bilateral and side meetings with heads of state and government, senior international officials and representatives of international organisations.
He held bilateral meetings with the leaders of Türkiye, Iran, Pakistan, Croatia, Haiti, Bhutan and Thailand, as well as senior officials from Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Sweden.
The meetings focused on bilateral relations, trade and investment, economic cooperation, manpower, the Rohingya crisis and regional and international issues.
The Prime Minister also met UN Secretary-General António Guterres, World Bank President Ajay Banga, UN officials and other international dignitaries.
In his UNGA address, Tarique highlighted Bangladesh’s priorities on global peace and security, climate change, sustainable development, economic cooperation and the Rohingya crisis.
He also outlined the government’s three-R strategy—Recovery, Restoration and Reconstruction—to rebuild Bangladesh.
During the visit, the Prime Minister also attended high-level events on the Rohingya crisis, sea-level rise, climate action and a just transition, and integrating midwifery into primary healthcare.
On the economic front, he attended a breakfast meeting hosted by JPMorgan Chase with Wall Street representatives, where he said Bangladesh is “open for business” and invited global investors to invest in the country.

item.title: Bangladesh, Turkiye discuss PM's participation in COP31
item.description:
Bangladesh and Turkiye have discussed the possible participation of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in COP31, to be hosted by Turkiye in Antalya.
The discussion took place when State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir met Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Friday on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, according to a Foreign Ministry press release.

item.description:
Development partners and countries provided Bangladesh with USD 294.5 million in loans in the first two months of the current fiscal year (July-August).

Meanwhile, Bangladesh had to repay nearly USD 700 million in principal and interest on previously borrowed loans during the same period.

The amount repaid was 237 per cent higher than the amount received in loans. Foreign loan disbursements in July-August were equivalent to 40 per cent of the amount disbursed during the same period last year.

Terms eased for foreign loans to foreign companies, borrowing costs to fall

The Economic Relations Division (ERD) published an updated report on the foreign loan situation for July-August today, Sunday. The report contains this information.

According to ERD sources, Bangladesh received a total of USD 750 million in foreign loans in July-August last year. This year, it received USD 294.5 million during the same period. The entire amount was provided by development partners and countries as project loans.

The Asian Development Bank (ADB) provided the largest amount, USD 128.7 million. The World Bank provided USD 73.9 million, while Japan provided nearly USD 40 million.

Foreign investment rises on reinvestment and intercompany loans

Foreign loan repayments have increased significantly over the past few years. In July-August of the current fiscal year, Bangladesh had to repay USD 698.9 million. Of this, USD 516 million was principal and more than USD 182.8 million was interest.

During the same period last year, the government had to repay around USD 670 million in principal and interest on foreign loans.

In July-August, Bangladesh received commitments for only USD 240 million in foreign loans. The amount was also USD 240 million during the same period last year.

item.title: Failure to curb land grabbing, extortion a bad omen for ruling party: TIB
item.description:
Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) has expressed deep concern and anger over the looting and vandalism at the Radda MCH-FP Health Centre in Mirpur and the vandalism of a content creator’s office in the ECB Chattar area in the capital.

Describing the incidents not as isolated events but as a bad omen for the government and the ruling party, the organisation called for exemplary accountability for those involved and urged the party to launch a nationwide campaign to put its own house in order.

TIB made the call in a statement on Sunday.

In the statement, TIB said, “The looting, vandalism and forcible occupation of Radda MCH are an embarrassing example for the government and the ruling party.”

TIB Executive Director Iftekharuzzaman said in the statement, “What kind of example is the ruling party setting by destroying, in the presence of police and before hundreds of people, a charitable organisation that has provided healthcare to poor and vulnerable mothers and children for half a century, allegedly under the patronage of a member of parliament’s reserved seat? Following the fall of an authoritarian kleptocracy through the bloody July uprising, what message are such activities by leaders and activists of the party that came to power through the people’s mandate in a historic election sending to the people? The memory of the arbitrary behaviour of the previous authoritarian government remains fresh in the minds of ordinary people. Against this backdrop, are BNP policymakers considering the consequences of the ongoing land grabbing and extortion by a significant section of the party’s leaders and activists?”

Iftekharuzzaman said widespread allegations of land grabbing, extortion and attempts to establish dominance had emerged against a section of the BNP after August 2024. He alleged that such activities were taking place in various sectors, including bus terminals, footpaths, markets, water bodies, sand quarries, bazaars, cable and internet businesses.

He said disputes and clashes were also taking place among party members over these activities, which he described as a bad omen for the government.

Referring to clashes between two local BNP factions over the occupation of a water body in Kishoreganj and the vandalism of a creative studio, TIB’s executive director said these were not isolated incidents but part of a continuing pattern of events since August 2024.

Iftekharuzzaman said land grabbing and extortion could spiral out of control unless the government took effective corrective measures immediately.

The TIB executive director said that although some measures, including expulsion from the party, had been taken, law enforcement agencies were unable to take effective action because of a lack of strong resistance and the direct or indirect links between the accused and the ruling party.

This, he said, had raised concerns that a culture of arbitrariness, corruption and impunity could return. TIB called for proper investigations into each incident and exemplary punishment for those found responsible.

item.title: Economy suffers from shortage of fresh Taka notes
item.description:
There is a severe shortage of new banknotes of all denominations in the market.
In contrast, the market is currently flooded with torn, damaged, punctured, and dirty unusable notes.
Although Bangladesh Bank releases new notes somewhat regularly, supply remains far short of demand.
Added to this is a shortage of low-denomination notes. Bank customers, shopkeepers, and shoppers in the market are feeling the lack of Tk100, Tk20, and Tk10 notes the most in daily transactions.
The situation has reached a point where customers often fail to get change even after withdrawing money from banks. The ordeal is worse at ATM booths.
Even when withdrawing Tk20,000, there is no guarantee of getting Tk500 notes.
In some booths, nineteen Tk1,000 notes are disbursed alongside two Tk500 notes.
As a result, despite having cash in hand, people have to run from store to store just to get change.
Meanwhile, a major portion of the banknotes circulating in the market is old, torn, punctured, and dirty.
Even Tk500 and Tk1,000 notes frequently show large staple punctures, Scotch tape repairs, torn edges, and dirt. Many shopkeepers refuse to accept these notes.
Ticket vending machines at metro rail stations or Cash Recycling Machines (CRMs) at banks often reject old and damaged notes as well.
Consequently, money received in one hand creates new trouble when trying to spend it with the other.
Recently, while attempting to deposit Tk50,000 at a Dutch-Bangla Bank CRM in Moghbazar, Md Ali Ahmed had 15 notes rejected.
He said he had just withdrawn the cash from a neighboring bank, yet the machine would not take it—even though he urgently needed to send money home that very day for his father’s medical treatment.
It is not just general customers; merchants report the same issue. In their words, without Tk100, Tk20, and Tk10 notes on hand, returning change for small purchases becomes extremely difficult.
Even banks often fail to supply low-denomination notes as requested. As a result, procuring change has become a separate task altogether for shopkeepers.
High printing costs
Amidst this, Bangladesh Bank data shows that money printing costs have hit a record high.
In FY26, Tk458.92 crore was spent on printing new currency, compared to Tk234.78 crore in the previous fiscal.
In just one year, printing expenses rose by Tk224 crore, or 95.46%. This marks the highest expenditure in the last five fiscal years.
In FY21, banknote printing cost roughly Tk340 crore, which dropped to Tk235 crore in FY25 before surging to nearly Tk459 crore a year later.
Sources at Bangladesh Bank stated that after August 5, 2024, the printing and release of old-design banknotes bearing the image of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman were halted.
Delays in the design, approval, and printing process of new note series led to a supply deficit of fresh notes in the market.
Arief Hossain Khan, executive director and spokesperson of Bangladesh Bank, noted that new Tk10, Tk500, and Tk1,000 taka notes have been released into the market. However, there is a supply shortage of raw materials for Tk20 and Tk50 notes, alongside rising printing costs overall.
He believes introducing digital transactions everywhere could serve as an effective solution, which is why the use of "Bangla QR" is being actively promoted. Expanding its reach would quickly reduce the demand for and usage of physical cash.
However, the reality remains that daily shopping and small transactions in the country are still heavily reliant on cash.
Victims of this situation believe that unless the supply of both fresh, quality banknotes and low-denomination currency normalize together, public suffering will not subside.
According to Bangladesh Bank, nearly all essential materials for printing notes—including security paper, specialized ink, security threads, and various chemicals—must be imported from abroad.
Even after raw materials arrive in the country, the printing process at the Security Printing Corporation (Bangladesh) takes nearly three months.
Due to limited capacity, the mint cannot print notes in required volumes all at once.
Furthermore, rising costs of raw materials, shipping, and the US dollar following the Russia-Ukraine war have pushed these expenses even higher.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,096 as nine die in 24 hours
item.description:
Nine more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Sunday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,096.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all nine of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 995, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 101, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the nine new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with four deaths reported in both the Dhaka division and Dhaka district.
A total of 1,228 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Sunday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 188,041.
During the same period, 113 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 21,212.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 166,310 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 159,519 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: BB governor: Int’l agreements being signed to identify, freeze laundered assets
item.description:
Initiatives have been taken to amend the "Distressed Asset Management Act" and the "Money Loan Court Act" to allow for judicial settlement within six months in order to curb defaulted loans and money laundering, announced Bangladesh Bank governor Md Mostaqur Rahman.
He stated that agreements are being made at the international level to identify and freeze assets laundered out of the country.
Additionally, 11 special joint investigation teams have been formed on the initiative of Bangladesh Bank.
He made these remarks as the chief guest at an exchange-of-views meeting titled "Implementation of Incentive Packages Announced by Bangladesh Bank for Private Sector Development" held at Bangladesh Agricultural University (BAU) on Saturday (September 26).
The event was organized at the university's Syed Nazrul Islam Conference Hall under the initiative of Bangladesh Bank to raise public awareness and inform stakeholders about the package.
Regarding the recovery of the country's fragile economy, Mostaqur Rahman noted that except for foreign exchange reserves, almost all economic indicators were in a risky and negative state when he assumed office.
Multiple special plans have been undertaken for economic recovery and bringing back laundered money. At the same time, effective measures are being taken to address irregularities and looting in the banking sector.
Regarding the distribution of low-interest funds, he stated that idle bank deposits are being utilized to provide funds at 4% interest.
These funds will be distributed to the SME and agriculture sectors at interest rates between 7% and 8%.
Furthermore, the process of launching a new fund to create young entrepreneurs is underway.
Plans include offering entrepreneurs a 50% grant and loans at interest rates of 4% to 5%.
Beneficiaries will be selected through a completely transparent process involving successful private sector entrepreneurs.
In the first session of the event, attendees were briefed on the incentive package announced by Bangladesh Bank, followed by an open Q&A session where bank officials and entrepreneurs from various levels raised their issues and inquiries.
During the meeting, organizers detailed the bank-announced incentive package, stating that this entrepreneur search program will initially be conducted across 64 upazilas from 8 divisions.
Ten individuals will be identified initially from each upazila, totaling 640. Phased over time, a total of 5,000 young entrepreneurs will be brought under this financing scheme.
Based on their needs, entrepreneurs will receive a financing package of up to maximum Tk20 lakh at a profit rate of 4% to 7%, comprising 50% bank loan and 50% grant.
Presided over by Md Arifuzzaman, executive director of Bangladesh Bank's Mymensingh region, special guests included Prof GM Mujibur Rahman, student affairs adviser of the university, and SM Humayun Kabir Sarkar, Mymensingh Divisional Commissioner.
Faculty members from various university departments, senior bank officials, and entrepreneurs from different areas of Mymensingh were also present at the event.

item.title: Seven Islamic parties differ over leadership, alliance conditions
item.description:
Although discussions on the framework for a proposed political alliance among seven Qawmi-oriented Islamic parties have made progress, the parties have failed to reach agreement on several key conditions. They remain divided over who will serve as convener and member secretary of the seven-party alliance, how leadership will change after the committee’s term ends, and what would happen if a party is part of another political alliance or wants to join a new alliance in the future. As a result, the unity of the seven parties has not yet been finalised.

However, it has been decided to form a 24-member liaison committee to advance the unity process. Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh Secretary General Allama Sajidur Rahman has been named convener of the liaison committee. The committee will include three leaders from each of the seven parties, along with two additional Hefazat leaders.

The seven parties have been asked to send the names of their representatives to Hefazat’s secretary general within two days. A meeting is scheduled to be held in Dhaka on 22 October to finalise the framework for the alliance.

The seven parties involved in the unity process are Islami Andolan Bangladesh, Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam Bangladesh, Khelafat Majlis, Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis, Bangladesh Khelafat Andolan, Islami Oikya Jote and Bangladesh Nezam-e-Islam Party.

Speaking to Prothom Alo by phone on Sunday evening, Islami Andolan Secretary General Gazi Ataur Rahman said everyone had expressed their views at the meeting. Considerable progress had been made towards forming the alliance, but a liaison committee was formed because some issues required further review.

According to meeting sources, representatives of the seven parties began their meeting at 11am on Sunday at Al-Jamiatul Islamia Azizul Ulum Babunagar Madrasa in Fatikchhari, Chattogram. The meeting was chaired by Hefazat-e-Islam Amir Allama Shah Muhibbullah Babunagari. Five representatives from each of the seven parties, a total of 35, attended the meeting.

Secretary General of the Qawmi madrasa education board Befaqul Madarisil Arabia Bangladesh Maulana Muhammad Mahfuzul Haque and leaders of a subcommittee formed by Hefazat-e-Islam to finalise the alliance were also present. The meeting continued until 1pm.

At the beginning of the meeting, the subcommittee presented a draft framework. Each party was then given half an hour to discuss the framework within its own forum. The parties subsequently presented their views. However, there were differences over several provisions.

Hefazat-e-Islam had formed a seven-member subcommittee to work on the alliance. Its members are Hefazat Secretary General Sajidur Rahman, senior mufti of Chattogram’s Hathazari Madrasa Allama Jasim Uddin, Hefazat Naib-e-Amirs Abdul Hamid, also known as Madhupur Pir, and Salahuddin Nanupuri, organising secretary Mufti Bashir Ullah, Narayanganj district president Maulana Abdul Awal, and Hefazat Amir’s son Mufti Ayub Babunagari.

The subcommittee collected proposals on the alliance framework from all the parties and then prepared a draft. The discussion on Sunday focused on that draft framework.

Asked about the meeting, Mufti Bashir Ullah told Prothom Alo that the unity process among the seven parties had advanced considerably. A liaison committee had been formed to discuss some issues further, and the committee would finalise the framework for the alliance.

Issues over which the parties differ

According to meeting sources, the draft framework for the seven-party alliance was presented at the outset. The parties then discussed it among themselves and gave their views. Representatives of each party subsequently presented their individual proposals and objections.

The discussions covered who would initially serve as convener and member secretary of the seven-party alliance, how the committee would be changed every six months, and what conditions would apply if a party was already part of another political alliance or wanted to join another alliance in the future. As the parties could not reach a consensus on these issues, the framework could not be finalised.

Several leaders involved in the unity process said the nature of alliances and political understandings among parties in Bangladesh changes over time. Therefore, they said, it needs further consideration whether it would be realistic to impose a condition barring any party from maintaining relations with another political party or alliance.

A senior leader of one of the parties told Prothom Alo on condition of anonymity that the parties had not been given the draft framework before the meeting. They received it at Sunday’s meeting, so some issues would need to be discussed within their respective party forums before decisions could be made.

Questions over Hefazat’s role

There are also discussions among the parties over how much of a role Hefazat-e-Islam should have in the seven-party unity process. Some leaders believe Hefazat should step back from the decision-making process once the alliance is finalised. They argue that Hefazat is a non-political organisation and that political parties should retain autonomy over their strategic decisions.

A senior leader of one of the parties told Prothom Alo on condition of anonymity that direct involvement of a non-political organisation in the decision-making of political parties could create complications. Hefazat could remain as a “shadow” over the alliance to prevent disputes or disorder among the parties, the leader said. However, political parties should retain independence in decision-making.

Constitution amendment bill likely in January, referendum proposed
item.description:
The government plans to introduce a bill to amend the Constitution in Parliament's first session in January next year, with a special committee aiming to submit its recommendations by December.
The proposed amendments may include provisions requiring a referendum on key constitutional changes, including amendments to the Constitution's preamble, Article 142 and provisions relating to the caretaker government system.
Home Minister and Chairman of the Special Committee on Constitution Amendment Salahuddin Ahmed said the proposed amendments requiring a referendum would be put to a public vote before receiving the president's assent.
He made the remarks at a press briefing following a meeting of the committee at the National Parliament Building on Sunday.
Salahuddin said the committee was working to submit its report to Parliament by December.
Based on the report, the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs would prepare and introduce the amendment bill.
"We are trying to place the report in Parliament by December. The bill may be introduced during the first session of Parliament in January next year," he said.
Explaining the proposed referendum mechanism, the home minister said constitutional amendments involving fundamental provisions would require a referendum before the president gave assent.
He identified the Constitution's preamble, Article 142 and other relevant constitutional provisions as areas where changes could trigger the requirement.
Salahuddin further said referendums could generally be divided into two categories: constitutional referendums and referendums on matters of law.
He added that no constitutional provision explicitly prohibits referendums on issues other than constitutional amendments.
Under the proposed arrangement, amendments passed by Parliament that require a referendum would be put to a public vote before being sent to the president for assent.
If voters approve the amendments, the president would then give assent, he said.
The home minister said Article 142 previously included a provision for a referendum on constitutional amendments, but the provision was abolished through the 15th Amendment during the Awami League government.
He said the referendum provision had been restored following a Supreme Court verdict in a case challenging the 15th Amendment after the August 5, 2024 uprising.
The proposed mechanism would bring constitutional amendments requiring public approval under a referendum process before they could receive presidential assent.
The legal implications and implementation of the restored provision will be central to the committee's recommendations.
The special committee has also proposed making a referendum mandatory for changes to constitutional provisions relating to the caretaker government system.
Salahuddin said his party had proposed at the National Consensus Commission that future parliaments should not be able to alter the caretaker government system without a referendum.
The proposal also seeks to require a referendum if any future parliament attempts to amend the relevant constitutional provisions.
He said the BNP had also proposed making referendums mandatory for changes to these provisions.
The proposal is intended to ensure that any future changes to the caretaker government system are subject to public approval.
The committee has repeatedly invited opposition parties to participate in the constitutional amendment process, Salahuddin said.
He said the committee would discuss the opposition's views and proposals if they joined its deliberations.
"Any acceptable proposals can be incorporated through discussions and based on the opinions of all parties," he said.
However, he acknowledged that the committee had no authority to compel opposition parties to participate and could only invite them and hope for their involvement.
The committee wants to ensure participation from political parties and other stakeholders in the process of amending the Constitution.
Sunday's meeting also included editors of national newspapers, senior journalists and representatives of various journalists' forums, who shared their views on proposed constitutional amendments.
The discussions covered a range of issues, including the Constitution's preamble, various articles and schedules.
The committee also invited participants to submit their proposals in writing for consideration.
The consultations are part of the committee's efforts to gather opinions from different professional groups and stakeholders before finalising its recommendations.
Salahuddin said the July National Charter would receive priority in the constitutional amendment process, while commitments made in the BNP's election manifesto would also be considered.
He said the committee would examine issues included in the July Charter as well as proposals that were not incorporated into the document or failed to secure consensus.
The committee has formally written to political parties to seek their participation in discussions on constitutional reform.
It aims to involve all relevant stakeholders, including parties that signed the July National Charter, in the process.
The committee is working to submit its report to Parliament by December, after which the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs will prepare the constitutional amendment bill.
The bill is expected to be introduced during Parliament's first session in January next year.
Following its introduction, the bill will undergo parliamentary discussions, during which lawmakers may propose amendments or raise objections.
The proposed constitutional changes will then proceed through the required parliamentary and constitutional procedures.
Amendments requiring a referendum would be put to a public vote before being sent to the president for assent.

item.title: PKSF to provide Tk7,245cr in financing for microenterprises, solar power
item.description:
Palli Karma-Sahayak Foundation (PKSF) has taken an initiative to provide a total of Tk7,245 crore in financing to promote renewable energy use and foster new entrepreneurship in the cottage and microenterprise sectors.
Of the total amount, Tk500 crore will be allocated for expanding rooftop solar power generation, said a press release.
The decisions were taken at a meeting of the PKSF Board of Directors held on Sunday at PKSF Bhaban-1 with PKSF Chairman Zakir Ahmed Khan in the chair.
Managing Director (MD) Md Fazlul Kader and other board members attended the meeting.
The board approved Tk5,000 crore in Bangladesh Bank-financed loans to support the creation of new entrepreneurs in the cottage and microenterprise sectors.
The financing will support technology-driven agriculture and agro-processing, manufacturing, services and various value-chain-based activities at the grassroots level.
The initiative aims to utilize the skills and productive capacity of low-income communities to create new entrepreneurs and expand employment opportunities, according to the PKSF.
Meanwhile, PKSF has launched a specialized financing program, backed by a Tk500 crore government allocation, to expand rooftop solar power generation.
Under the program, the board approved a specialized lending policy titled 'Shouro Shokti' to provide loans to customers through partner organizations at an interest rate of 6%.
The board also approved nearly Tk2,000 crore in loans for PKSF's partner organizations to support cluster-based microenterprises, general services, the ultra-poor, agriculture and other sectors.

item.title: Greek EU presidency eyes migrant return hub in Africa: Minister
item.description:
Greece said Monday it aimed to set up a hub in Africa for sending back migrants once it takes up the EU presidency in 2027.

"We believe that the framework is opening up under the Greek presidency for the return centre to operate," Greece's migration minister Thanos Plevris told ANT1 TV.

He added that the hub would run "in an African country that we have already agreed on; we simply cannot name it yet."

Greece will hold the rotating presidency of the European Union in the second half of 2027.

Uganda and Rwanda have been cited as possible sites, with EU states Denmark, Austria, Germany and the Netherlands working with Greece on the initiative.

Plevris said a meeting will soon be organised with the other four EU states and the director of the International Organisation for Migration to discuss the plan.

The European Parliament in June approved a regulation on the return of migrants whose asylum claims have been rejected, including the possibility for member states to conclude agreements to establish detention centres outside the union's borders.

This regulation, intended to speed up expulsions, has raised concerns among human rights advocates.

The Council of Europe, the continent's human rights watchdog, has sent letters to the commissioners responsible for migration policy in these five countries, submitting recommendations to them to address potential human rights violations.

Plevris also said that Greece wants to present at the next European Council on Home Affairs on 1 October "a mechanism of exceptional measures" in the event of an influx crisis such as the recent events in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, where 72,000 migrants crossed the border from Morocco.

"In times of crisis, measures outside the box must be taken," he said.

"In these cases where we have instrumentalisation (of migration), and we have experienced it with mass flows that we have prevented, then not only should asylum not even be considered, there should be an immediate issuance of a return decision and immediate return," Plevris said.

Greece has twice suspended the registration of asylum applications: in March 2020 during a crisis at the Greek-Turkish border, and in July 2025 during a large influx to Crete of migrants coming from Libya.

item.title: Banglalink brings mobile services to ChatGPT
item.description:
Banglalink has brought its core mobile services into ChatGPT in the first such integration by a telecom operator in Bangladesh, allowing customers to access everyday mobile services through a simple conversation, reports a press release.

With Banglalink GPT, subscribers can manage everyday telco needs directly through ChatGPT, from checking their balance and usage and finding suitable packs to checking roaming status and accessing other key mobile services, without having to switch between different apps or websites.

Developed by Banglalink Digital, the service is now live nationwide for Banglalink subscribers. They can find Banglalink GPT in ChatGPT’s GPT section and use it by simply asking questions in everyday language.

Banglalink GPT also recommends suitable packs to users based on their needs and usage. For instance, a customer planning to watch a movie can ask which pack would be suitable, while another can ask to check their current balance, minutes or internet data.

Customers can also check their roaming status through the assistant. For services that require a transaction, customers can complete the process through Banglalink’s payment portal.

Taimur Rahman, chief corporate & regulatory affairs Officer of Banglalink, said, “Customer expectations are evolving rapidly as AI becomes increasingly integrated into everyday life. At Banglalink, we believe that accessing and managing mobile services should evolve accordingly. By becoming the first telecom operator in Bangladesh to bring our services into ChatGPT, we are making it easier for customers to discover, manage, and purchase the services they need through a familiar conversational interface. This initiative reflects our commitment to using technology to make digital experiences more intuitive, accessible, and customer-centric”

The new service is part of Banglalink’s broader effort as a digital operator to make everyday services simpler and more accessible through technology.

item.title: Bangladesh wants to join trade bloc RCEP, what could it gain
item.description:
Bangladesh’s bid to join the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), one of the world’s largest free trade blocs, has moved a step forward. Trade ministers from the bloc’s member countries have approved a recommendation to form a special task force to advance formal discussions and technical procedure involving Bangladesh and three other applicant countries.

Alongside Bangladesh, Chile, Sri Lanka and Hong Kong have applied to join the 15-country trade bloc in the Asia-Pacific region. At a meeting of the RCEP Joint Committee in Manila on 21 September, a recommendation was made to form a special task force for the applicant countries. The recommendation was later approved at the fifth RCEP Ministerial Meeting, also held in the Philippine capital, Manila.

RCEP is a bloc comprising 15 countries, including China, Japan and South Korea. Trade among its member countries was worth around USD 2.1 trillion. Becoming an RCEP member could create opportunities for Bangladesh to receive preferential trade benefits in the markets of member countries.

Efforts are underway to sign as many trade agreements as possible before LDC graduation

It would also cover areas such as services, investment, intellectual property, e-commerce, competition, dispute settlement and support for small and medium-sized enterprises.

Bangladesh began initial efforts and discussions to join RCEP in 2022. Two months after the interim government led by Professor Muhammad Yunus took office, it sent a letter in October 2024 expressing its interest. RCEP at the time however, had not yet decided on admitting new members.

In 2025, RCEP members approved a process for admitting new countries. Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Chile and Hong Kong subsequently submitted formal applications. As part of the formal application process for joining RCEP, Bangladesh has already submitted the required documents.

At a joint press conference with the prime minister of Malaysia last June, Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman said Bangladesh was interested in joining RCEP and welcomed Malaysia’s support on the matter. Bangladesh has also sought Australia’s support in this regard.

Sources at the Ministry of Commerce said the task force will work to advance formal discussions and the technical process with Bangladesh and the other interested countries, in line with the roadmap for expanding the bloc and admitting new members.

Commerce Secretary Md Ataur Rahman Khan told Prothom Alo, “We want to become a member of RCEP. The good news is that at the RCEP Joint Committee meeting last Monday, we received a positive indication regarding membership for all four countries, including Bangladesh. As Bangladesh’s process of graduating from the least developed country (LDC) category moves forward, we will benefit if we can become a member of the bloc.”

Experts say joining RCEP is important for Bangladesh mainly because of the opportunities it could create for tariff benefits in export markets and trade expansion. After graduating from the LDC category, Bangladesh may lose tariff benefits in various countries.

Becoming an RCEP member could create opportunities to receive preferential trade benefits in the markets of bloc members. Alongside benefits in goods trade, the agreement would also cover services, investment, intellectual property, e-commerce, competition, dispute settlement and support for small and medium-sized enterprises.

Bangladesh hopeful of signing FTA with Malaysia by 2027

Bangladesh will gain tariff benefits, but must offer them too

Officials at the Ministry of Commerce say Bangladesh joining RCEP could play an important role in addressing the challenges following graduation from the LDC category, retaining tariff benefits in international trade, strengthening links with global supply chains and attracting foreign direct investment to the country.

Who are RCEP’s members, and how much they trade

RCEP currently comprises the 10 members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN): Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. There are five other countries: China, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand.

The bloc represents around 30 per cent of global gross domestic product (GDP) and population. In 2024, trade among its member countries was worth around USD 2.1 trillion.

According to a report by the Bangladesh Trade and Tariff Commission, RCEP countries account for 53.90 per cent of Bangladesh’s total imports and 7.92 per cent of its exports. In other words, becoming a member of the bloc could create an opportunity for Bangladesh to further institutionalise its trade relations with major import and export markets.

‘Bangladesh will have to negotiate skilfully’

It is learnt that Bangladesh would need the consent of all 15 existing RCEP members to join the bloc. It would also have to demonstrate its ability to comply with the agreement’s rules and regulations and offer market access to member countries.

Bangladesh’s main tasks now, therefore, are to negotiate its membership, make proposals on market access and bargain over various terms of the agreement. Key issues include how much tariff preference will be granted on which products, how quickly those preferences will be implemented and what kind of market access Bangladesh will have to offer.

How new US tariff will affect Bangladesh’s trade

The Manila meeting reportedly emphasised strengthening regional economic integration through cooperation and constructive dialogue among member countries. It also stressed the need to remove unnecessary barriers to international trade and to put emphasis on the World Trade Organization (WTO) reform process.

Mustafizur Rahman, distinguished fellow at the private research organisation Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD), told Prothom Alo that after graduating from the LDC category, Bangladesh would need to pursue free trade agreements (FTAs) and comprehensive economic partnership agreements (CEPAs) with various countries. From that perspective, joining a trade bloc such as RCEP would be beneficial for Bangladesh.

“Bangladesh has initiatives under way to sign FTAs with some countries. At the same time, among RCEP members there are some strong economies as well as some weaker ones. Alongside receiving trade benefits, members also have to provide benefits to other member countries. That is the main challenge. Bangladesh will have to negotiate skilfully to address this challenge. I would like to have confidence that Bangladesh will do so,” he added.

item.title: Salauddin: No journalist to be victimized under Cyber Security law
item.description:
The government is exercising utmost caution so that the proposed Cyber Security (Amendment) Act does not become an oppressive law and that no journalist or media outlet is victimized under it, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said on Monday.
The proposed law would be finalized only after extensive consultations with stakeholders and consideration of their recommendations, he said at a press briefing at the Secretariat following a consultation meeting with representatives of print and electronic media at the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
“Our primary objective is to ensure that no journalist falls victim to the misuse of this law,” he said.
The home minister said the draft amendment bill was earlier laid before the Cabinet, which directed the authorities to hold extensive discussions with IT experts and other stakeholders involved in cyberspace.
Then the government published the draft on its website to seek opinions from people from all walks of life, he said, adding that feedback has already been received from various institutions, human rights organisations, students and cyberspace users.
Monday’s meeting was the government’s second consultation with editors, senior journalists, newspaper organisations and representatives of professional journalists’ associations.
At the first meeting on September 10, editors were requested to submit their views in writing or through the website.
The minister said many participants presented their views at Monday’s meeting and pledged to submit written recommendations.
He said a proposal came to hold detailed discussions between media and cyber experts to ensure that the media is not harmed or victimised and that necessary safeguards are incorporated into the law.
“The government has gladly accepted the proposal,” Salahuddin said, adding that the government has no intention of enacting the law to target the media.
Regarding safeguards for journalists in print, electronic and online media, the minister said a proposal was made to make prior court approval mandatory before taking action against or arresting a journalist.
He said the government considered the proposal appropriate and logical.
Stakeholders will be given another 15 days to submit formal recommendations, which will then be considered for inclusion in the draft, he said.
A provision setting a specific timeframe for the disposal of cases or appeals will also be considered to prevent people from remaining in legal uncertainty for an indefinite period, the minister added.
Salahuddin said a special coordination mechanism would be formed to help finalise the draft.
The Principal Information Officer will serve as the focal point, while the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting will jointly coordinate the process.
Representatives of the Editors’ Council, Electronic Media Association and a panel of cyber experts formed by the IT ministry will participate in the process and are expected to submit recommendations within 7 to 15 days, said the minister.
The revised draft will then be published on the government website again for further public feedback before being placed before the Cabinet, the minister added.
If the recommendations are accepted, they will be incorporated into the draft before an inter-ministerial review and submission to the Cabinet.
After Cabinet approval, the bill will be placed before Parliament where it will undergo further deliberation involving members of both the ruling and opposition parties as well as views emerging from seminars and symposiums outside Parliament.
Salahuddin said the main objective of the proposed law is to establish a balanced legal framework to protect the country, society and young people from cybercrimes and other criminal activities.
The act is also intended to comply with international standards while protecting social and religious harmony, family values and indigenous culture, he said.

item.title: Gold prices drop further
item.description:
The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (Bajus) has reduced gold prices again, with the price of 22-carat gold falling by Tk185 per gram.
Under the new rates, 22-carat hallmarked gold will cost Tk19,785 per gram, including VAT.
The new prices came into effect at 10am on Monday, following another reduction announced by Bajus on Saturday.
The Bajus Standing Committee on Pricing and Price Monitoring set the new rates at a meeting at 9am on Monday. The decision was announced in a notification signed by the committee’s chairman, Dr Dewan Aminul Islam Shahin.
The price of one bhori (11.664 grams) of 22-carat gold now stands at approximately Tk230,770, including VAT. Making charges will be added separately depending on the design of the jewellery.
The price of 21-carat gold has been set at Tk18,895 per gram, while 18-carat gold will cost Tk16,225 per gram. Gold sold under the traditional method has been priced at Tk13,225 per gram.
On September 26, the price of 22-carat gold stood at Tk19,970 per gram, including VAT. The price per bhori was reduced by Tk1,691 that day.
With Monday’s reduction, the price of 22-carat gold has fallen by approximately Tk2,159 per bhori over two days.
Bajus has also reduced the prices of silver jewellery.
Under the new rates, 22-carat silver will cost Tk385 per gram, 21-carat silver Tk370, 18-carat silver Tk320 and traditional-method silver Tk240 per gram.
The price of 22-carat silver was Tk415 per gram on September 26, meaning it has fallen by Tk30 per gram in two days.
Bajus said making charges will be applicable separately based on the design of the jewellery.
However, as VAT is already included in the fixed selling price, it cannot be charged separately from customers.
For exchanges involving old gold jewellery, 12% will be deducted from the gold price, excluding making charges and the cost of stones. For purchases of old jewellery, the deduction will be 18%.
VAT cannot be deducted separately in either exchange or purchase transactions, according to Bajus.
The new rates will remain in effect at jewellery shops across the country until further notice.
Bajus said the decision was taken after reviewing the overall market situation, including a decline in the prices of raw gold and silver.

item.title: Bangladesh lose to Singapore 1-0 in Asean Cup
item.description:
Bangladesh suffered a 1-0 defeat to Singapore in their second Group A match of the FIFA Asean Cup 2026 at the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Monday.
Harhys Stewart scored the only goal in the first half, which proved decisive as Singapore secured their third straight victory over Bangladesh.
Following a cross from Nur Adam Abdullah, Harhys headed home in the 35th minute after Bangladesh goalkeeper Mehedi Hasan Srabon had made a couple of important saves.
Srabon first denied Ilhan Fandi with a diving save in the 17th minute before rescuing Bangladesh from a goalmouth scramble in the 33rd minute.
The men in red and green piled on the pressure in search of an equaliser throughout the second half but could not find the net, with headers from Shamit Shome and Saad Uddin missing the target.
Shamit's flying header from a Saad cross went over the bar, while Saad headed wide from substitute Fahamedul Islam's cross. Hamza Choudhury was pushed further forward in the closing stages, but Bangladesh could not find a way through.
Bangladesh coach Thomas Dooley made three changes to the starting XI that lost 3-0 to Malaysia in their tournament opener on Friday.
Centre-back Zidane Yousuf and midfielder Jamal Bhuiyan came into the lineup in place of Shakil Ahad Topu and Sohel Rana, while Sheikh Morsalin replaced Farhaan Ali Wahid, who made his international debut against Malaysia, in the forward line.
In the second half, Minhaz Shadin replaced Morsalin to make his international debut.
It was the third meeting between Bangladesh and Singapore in the last 15 months, with Singapore winning all three encounters.
Bangladesh have now recorded three draws and remain without a victory against the Southeast Asian side.
The men in red and green will face hosts and tournament favourites Indonesia in their final group-stage fixture at the same venue on Thursday.

item.title: BCB unveils annual domestic competition spanning three formats
item.description:
The Bangladesh Cricket Board unveiled a new three-format domestic tournament that will bring together T20, 50-over and four-day cricket under a single competition in an effort to increase interest in the country’s domestic game.
The tournament, called the Domestic Three Trophy, or D3 Trophy, will feature six teams owned by six corporate groups under three-year agreements with the BCB.
The six teams are backed by H. Bluestar, Walton Group, Citizens Bank, ACME Group, Seven Rings Cement and Fortune Group. The team owners include three BCB directors: Fahim Sinha of ACME Group, Mizanur Rahman of Fortune Group and Shahniyan Tanim of H. Bluestar.
The D3 Trophy will replace three of the BCB’s existing domestic competitions with a single structure. The four-day National Cricket League will remain separate, while the Bangladesh Cricket League’s four-day and one-day competitions and the NCL’s T20 competition will be incorporated into the new tournament.
The T20 competition will open the tournament on Dec. 15 at the renovated Jibanananda Das Cricket Stadium in Barishal. The BCB plans to gradually take the competition to all divisions. Khulna is being considered as the second venue, with Dhaka as an alternative.
The four-day matches will begin in January, followed by the 50-over competition in May. Across the three formats, the tournament will feature seven four-day matches, 16 one-day matches and 19 T20 matches.
Each team will be allowed to sign up to 23 players for all three formats. Coaching staff, analysts, physiotherapists and trainers will also be selected through a draft.
The six teams announced their icon players at Sunday’s launch. Walton selected Mehedi Hasan Miraz, Fortune chose Towhid Hridoy, ACME took Mosaddek Hossain, Seven Rings Cement picked Mushfiqur Rahim, H. Bluestar selected Nurul Hasan and Citizens Bank named Mohammad Naim.
BCB President Tamim Iqbal said the board had been concerned by criticism that domestic cricket had lost its appeal.
“We often hear that domestic cricket has lost its color, that there is no interest and that some call it picnic cricket,” he said. “When we came to the board, we were concerned about this and thought about how we could bring that color back.”
Youth and Sports State Minister Aminul Haque said keeping domestic cricket active for six or seven months a year could help narrow the gap between players competing at domestic level and those in the national team.

item.title: Netherlands regrets Israel retaliation in settlements row
item.description:
The Netherlands said Monday it regretted Israel’s decision to revoke accreditation of Dutch diplomats based in the West Bank, the latest retaliation by Israel to mounting Western pressure over settlements.
Israel, which has occupied the West Bank since 1967 and exerts power over diplomats’ entry into the Palestinian territory, on Monday ordered Dutch officials to surrender their diplomatic privileges.
“I deeply regret this unnecessary decision,” Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen said.
Israel retaliated after Dutch authorities began implementing a ban on imports of any products from Israeli settlements in the West Bank.
The decision, Berendsen said, was “not directed against Israel.”
The minister said the suspension of the imports came from “the obligation, under international law, not to contribute to an unlawful situation: the illegal settlements.”
Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar, announcing the move on Sunday, vowed: “Any country that acts in a hostile and one-sided manner against Israel will lose its influence and relevance in the region.”
“If the Netherlands wishes to continue representing its interests vis-a-vis the Palestinians, it may do so from the territory of the Palestinian Authority and not from the territory of the State of Israel,” he said.
Israel controls entry points into the West Bank and the Oslo peace accords in the 1990s gave Israel control over diplomatic accreditation in the Palestinian territories.
The Palestinian Authority condemned the move, saying Israel was trying to “reduce the international and diplomatic presence in Palestine so that it can carry out its crimes without witnesses.”
“The State of Palestine affirms that Dutch diplomats are welcome on the territory of the occupied State of Palestine, and that Israel has no sovereignty over any part of the land of the State of Palestine,” the foreign ministry said.
The Dutch government imposed the sanctions in July out of alarm at the rising number of attacks by Israeli settlers on Palestinians and talk by Israeli politicians of formally annexing the territory.
Britain, France and Canada also announced in early September that they would impose sanctions on trade from Israeli settlements. Israel responded by ordering the closure of the British consulate in Jerusalem.
Ahead of Israeli elections on October 27, opposition figure Yair Lapid, a centrist former prime minister, said that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu bore responsibility for the “anti-Israel wave.”
“The fact that Israelis landing in the Netherlands are having their bags rummaged through and products from the settlements confiscated is a diplomatic failure unlike anything we have seen before,” Lapid said, promising improved diplomacy but not mentioning a change in policy on settlements.
The United Nations says extremist settlers have been responsible for an average of six attacks per day on Palestinians and Palestinian property in the West Bank in 2026.
Palestinians have also attacked Israelis, with a Palestinian shooting dead a settler last week and a car-ramming attack seriously injuring the soldier son of the Israeli ambassador to Washington.

item.title: Death toll in South Africa bar shooting rises to 18
item.description:
The death toll in a mass shooting in a South African tavern has risen to 18 after one person died in hospital, police said Monday, adding that at least two of the dead were Lesotho nationals.
The shooting west of Johannesburg late Saturday was part of a bloody weekend in the crime-weary country, with 10 people killed in another mass shooting in Cape Town on Sunday.
Eight gunmen armed with assault rifles stormed the bar in the semi-rural township of Wedela, around 80 kilometers (50 miles) from central Johannesburg, killing 13 men and four women, police said.
“One more victim has died in hospital, bringing the total number of deceased to 18,” they said Monday. Eighteen people were wounded.
“Only four of the deceased have been identified, two South Africans and two Lesotho nationals.”
The motive for the attack was not clear, but police said it may have been retaliation for an incident in the same tavern in August when one person was killed and another wounded.
The area was gripped by rivalry between gangs involved in illicit mining for gold, the tavern owner told local journalists at the scene, where bloodied clothes lay on the ground.
“Even if they finish investigating, I am scared to continue selling again. I am too scared,” she said, hiding her identity.
Thousands of unregistered miners operate in abandoned mining shafts in South Africa, in a sector linked to organized crime, assassinations and other illegal activities.
Many come from across southern Africa, including the kingdom of Lesotho which is embedded within South Africa.
In a separate shooting at the weekend, gunmen killed 10 people and wounded 11 more at an eating and drinking venue in a township outside Cape Town early on Sunday.
In video clips shared on social media, revelers can be seen dancing and drinking before a burst of gunfire rings out, sending people scrambling for cover.
Police said it was not clear what prompted the attack in Lwandle, but one official said it may have been business rivalry.
There had been no arrests in either of the mass killings.
South Africa is awash with legal and illegal firearms and shootings are common. The country of around 62 million people has one of the world’s highest murder rates, with about 60 people killed each day.
There have been at least 41 mass killings this year at the cost of 196 lives, said Julian Rademeyer, an adviser for the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime (GI-TOC).
“Very often these are killings that are linked to organized crime” including illegal mining, gang violence and extortion, he told the Newzroom Afrika broadcaster.
In March, President Cyril Ramaphosa deployed the army to violence hotspots around Johannesburg and Cape Town after describing organized crime the “most immediate threat” to South Africa’s democracy and economic development.
The weekend bloodshed further rattled South Africans already alarmed by the discovery of the bodies of 11 women, one of them on Sunday, in 10 weeks in Johannesburg’s Ekurhuleni area.
Most of the victims were in their 20s and 30s, with some found stripped of their clothes and showing signs of sexual assault, police said.
In the same area, a 23-year-old woman was shot and killed early Monday during an alleged robbery while she was on the way to work, police said.
“Preliminary investigations have not established any link between this incident and the recent cases involving the bodies of women found in Ekurhuleni,” they said in a statement.

item.title: Cabinet clears draft VAT law requiring returns within 15 days
item.description:
The Cabinet on Monday gave the final approval, subject to vetting by the Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, to a draft ordinance seeking to restore the provision requiring taxpayers to submit VAT returns within 15 days after the end of each tax period instead of every three tax periods.
The clearance was given to the draft Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026 at the cabinet meeting held with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in the chair at the Bangladesh Secretariat.
The draft law proposed amendment to section 64 of the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012, to bring greater dynamism to revenue collection at the field level.
Under the proposed provision, VAT returns will have to be submitted within 15 days of the end of each tax period, instead of the existing provision allowing submission within 15 days after the end of every three tax periods.
If the 15th day falls on a public holiday, the return may be submitted on the next working day.
The proposed amendment also provides additional time for certain taxpayers. Government, semi-government and autonomous bodies, banks, insurance companies, and individuals or entities submitting zero returns will be allowed to submit their returns within 20 days of the end of every tax period.
The Internal Resources Division placed the draft ordinance before the cabinet for both approval in-principle and final approval.

item.title: BB issues guidelines for dispute resolution in Bangla QR
item.description:
To make digital transactions safer, more transparent, and more customer-friendly, Bangladesh Bank has issued new guidelines for resolving disputes in Bangla QR (merchant payment) transactions.
The Payment Systems Department of the central bank issued a circular in this regard yesterday.
The guidelines will take effect on December 1.
According to the "Guidelines on Dispute Resolution for Bangla QR (Merchant Payment) Transactions," customers will not need to lodge a separate complaint for failed transactions. Once the system confirms a transaction failure, the money will be refunded automatically. If an immediate refund is not possible, it must be completed within a maximum of 30 minutes.
General disputes between customers and merchants using the same bank or MFS (Mobile Financial Services) provider must be resolved within three working days.
Meanwhile, transaction disputes involving different institutions will be settled through the NPSB's central Dispute Management System.
Customers can lodge complaints within 45 days of the transaction.
The issuing institution must communicate its decision within two working days.
The entire dispute resolution process, including chargebacks and arbitration if necessary, must be completed within a maximum of 30 days.
Additionally, in cases of QR code tampering, fraud, or unauthorized transactions, investigations must be completed within 30 days, and necessary refunds or compensation must be arranged.
Bangladesh Bank will take action under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2024 for non-compliance with these directions.

item.title: BB permits purchase of foreign airline tickets via credit cards
item.description:
Bangladesh Bank has allowed passengers to purchase tickets for foreign airlines operating in Bangladesh directly using international credit and debit cards.
As a result, in addition to traditional banking channels or travel agencies, passengers will now be able to pay for tickets directly using international cards.
On Monday (September 28), the Foreign Exchange Policy Department (FEPD-1) of Bangladesh Bank issued a circular in this regard and sent it to all authorized dealer (AD) banks.
The circular states that, subject to holding a valid visa, Bangladeshi citizens can use international cards to purchase tickets for foreign airlines operating in the country for overseas travel.
This facility will also apply to foreign airlines whose ticket sales proceeds are settled outside Bangladesh through international acquiring and payment settlement systems.
According to Bangladesh Bank instructions, this card-based ticket purchasing facility will remain outside the prescribed annual travel quota.
However, after verifying the authenticity of the ticket purchase, the respective bank can refill or adjust the funds used on the customer's card.
Banks must follow the specific Merchant Category Code (MCC) of the respective airline to identify such transactions.
However, this facility for purchasing tickets through foreign platforms will not apply to domestic airlines of Bangladesh.
That is, if a ticket for a Bangladeshi airline is purchased through a platform providing services from outside the country, this facility will not be available.
The circular further states that foreign currency earned from ticket sales must be calculated and adjusted as remittable surplus according to existing guidelines when remitting it to the airline's home country.
Additionally, information on these transactions must be regularly reported through Bangladesh Bank's TM (Transaction Monitoring) module.
The circular, signed by Md Abu Bakkarr Siddique, director of Bangladesh Bank (FEPD-1), has been ordered to take effect immediately.

item.title: Govt drafts market-specific export strategies for 18 key destinations
item.description:
The government is preparing an integrated strategy to diversify both products and markets, aiming to boost export earnings and reduce the country's heavy dependence on ready-made garments (RMG).
Under the initiative, separate market-based export strategies are being drafted for 18 key trading destinations worldwide, based on an analysis of market potential, existing barriers, competitors' positions and the steps Bangladesh needs to take.
Commerce secretary Ataur Rahman Khan announced the move while presiding over a workshop titled "Bangladesh Export Diversification Strategy: Product and Market Diversification Across 18 Key Trading Destinations" at the Secretariat on Monday.
"Equal importance is being given to both product diversification and market diversification to make Bangladesh's exports stronger and more sustainable," he said.
He said detailed country profiles and implementable strategies are being prepared after collecting and analyzing information on the 18 selected destinations.
Information on the current situation in the target markets, existing export barriers, Bangladesh's potential products and scope for trade expansion has been gathered from the country's commercial wings abroad, the secretary said. "A separate action plan will be drawn up for each country by consolidating this data."
Ataur said a specific matrix is being followed for market analysis. "It includes Bangladesh's share in the country's total imports, main competitors for specific products, ways to enhance competitiveness, and the policy and institutional measures needed for market expansion."
He added that the analysis of the 18 markets would help identify new potential products, expand markets for existing items and determine the steps required to enter new markets.
Speaking at the workshop, Mustafizur Rahman, Distinguished Fellow of the Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD), said services exports must receive equal priority alongside goods in any diversification drive.
He called for effective initiatives to develop information technology, the skills-based economy and enabling service sectors, along with support for the growth of freelancers.
Stressing skills development and technological upgrading, he said greater use of technology in manufacturing and services is essential to improve competitiveness in international markets.
He also suggested stepping up efforts to increase exports of Bangladeshi goods and services to neighbouring countries by leveraging geographical proximity.
Representatives of the BGMEA, Flexa, CPD, Walton Group, Bangladesh Agro-Processors' Association and the pharmaceutical sector, among others, placed their proposals for expanding exports at the workshop.
Officials from the Ministry of Commerce and other relevant ministries and organizations also attended.
Participants emphasized making sectors such as pharmaceuticals, electronics, agriculture and agro-processed products, leather and leather goods, light engineering, information technology and other services more competitive in global markets, alongside RMG.
Stakeholders said the strategy centred on the 18 destinations would play a key role in broadening the export base, creating new products and markets, deepening partnerships in existing markets and building a diversified, sustainable export structure in the long run.

item.title: Two dead, 14 missing after avalanche on Nepal’s Himlung peak
item.description:
At least two people have been killed and 14 remain missing after an avalanche at Nepal’s Himlung peak, an official said on Monday, as rescuers resumed their search.
The avalanche swept through the base camp of the 7,126-metre (23,345-foot) peak near the Chinese border early on Sunday, burying tents under deep snow.
“Two bodies were found as rescuers worked until 6pm last night,” Tul Singh Gurung, president of the Nepal National Mountain Guide Association, told AFP.
“The search continues for 14 expedition workers who are still missing.”
A team of eight mountain guides is involved in the search operation, he added.
Mountaineer Mingma G Sherpa, who is leading the rescue team, said challenging weather conditions were hampering their efforts.
“We could have saved lives but due to bad weather, we reached the accident site only in the evening (on Sunday),” he wrote on Facebook.
Sherpa said the deceased were both guides, while the 14 missing were kitchen staff working at the expedition camp.
Organizers initially reported that at least 10 people were missing.
It was the latest natural disaster to hit Nepal in recent weeks.
The Himalayan nation is rebuilding from a devastating glacial flood on August 26 that killed more than 1,400 people and left over 6,000 missing.
And heavy rain since Thursday has triggered other floods and landslides, killing at least 21 people, according to the national disaster agency.
Home to eight of the world’s 14 highest peaks, Nepal relies heavily on mountaineering and trekking tourism.

World Bank-funded Tk 13b project to reform banking sector
item.description:
The government is undertaking a new project to reform the country’s banking sector, strengthen supervisory capacity and enhance financial-sector safeguards. The project has an estimated cost of Tk 12.76 billion (1,276 crore).

The project will support the development of Bangladesh Bank’s technological infrastructure, bank restructuring, depositor protection and reforms at state-owned banks over five years. Titled the Financial Sector Support Project-2 (FSSP-2), Bangladesh Bank will implement the project.

The project is scheduled to be placed before the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) at its meeting in Dhaka’s Secretariat today, Tuesday. The agenda includes a total of 15 projects for approval, including this one.

Of the project’s total cost, the World Bank’s International Development Association (IDA) will provide Tk 12.61 billion (1,261 crore). Bangladesh Bank will finance the remaining Tk 140 million (14 crore) from its own resources. The project will run from July this year to June 2031.

Asked about the project, Planning Division Secretary SM Shakil Akhter told Prothom Alo, “The project has been taken up to address mismanagement in the financial sector. Through this project, technological development in the banking sector and procurement activities will be modernised and made more transparent. In addition, various reform measures will be implemented at the policy level.”

Why this project

According to the project proposal, the country’s banking sector has long suffered from high levels of non-performing loans, governance deficiencies and weak technological capacity.

Some banks are facing liquidity and capital shortages. Strengthening financial-sector safeguards and modernising the banking system are therefore essential to address these challenges.

Against this backdrop, the second phase of the project is being undertaken as a continuation of the earlier Financial Sector Support Project.

Officials concerned said the project would invest in improving information and communication technology (ICT) infrastructure to strengthen Bangladesh Bank’s supervisory capacity.

The plan includes installing necessary computers, technological equipment, software and databases.

The project will also provide training for officials involved in banking-sector supervision and engage consultants to strengthen institutional capacity.

Major activities

The project has been proposed for implementation in three phases. The first phase will focus on strengthening banking-sector supervisory capacity and developing technological infrastructure.

SM Shakil Akhter, Planning Division Secretary The project has been taken up to address mismanagement in the financial sector. Through this project, technological development in the banking sector and procurement activities will be modernised and made more transparent. In addition, various reform measures will be implemented at the policy level.

The second phase will strengthen financial-sector safeguards, support bank restructuring and reform state-owned banks. The third phase will provide the necessary administrative and technical support.

One of the project’s key objectives is to strengthen the banking sector’s financial safety net. To this end, initiatives will be taken to enhance the financial capacity of the Deposit Insurance Trust Fund (DITF).

At the same time, the project will strengthen institutional capacity to protect depositors during bank resolution or restructuring, reduce the time required to repay depositors and support bank restructuring activities.

The project will also focus on improving governance and financial stability at state-owned banks. It also plans to introduce performance-based conditions (PBCs) for bank restructuring and reform. In other words, the project will establish a mechanism to advance reforms based on specified actions and outcomes.

The project summary highlights the weaknesses in the country’s banking sector, noting that some banks, particularly state-owned and Islamic banks, have faced liquidity and capital shortages. Several banks have fallen into negative capital positions.

Meanwhile, outdated ICT infrastructure and the lack of integrated information management systems are limiting banking-sector supervision. These limitations also pose challenges in addressing cyberattacks and cross-border financial risks.

Project costs

A major portion of the project’s budget has been allocated to developing technological infrastructure. This includes a proposed allocation of Tk 7.11 billion (711 crore) for purchasing information and communication technology equipment and Tk 3.5536 billion (355.36 crore) for computer software.

Funds have also been earmarked for training, hiring consultants, developing databases and purchasing other technological equipment.

The project proposes an allocation of Tk 700 million (70 crore) for training. A total of 3,565 people will receive training under this component. The proposal includes Tk 290 million (29 crore) for hiring individual consultants and Tk 650 million (65 crore) for institutional consultancy services.

After reviewing the project proposal, the Planning Commission said its implementation would strengthen Bangladesh’s financial-sector safeguards. It would also help develop technology-driven banking and support reforms and restructuring in the banking sector.

First-phase work

Bangladesh Bank’s Financial Sector Support Project was approved in 2015. The project ran from September of that year to March 2021, with an initial estimated cost of US$300 million. The actual expenditure, however, amounted to US$262 million.

According to World Bank data, the first phase of the project covered three major areas. These included digital infrastructure for the financial sector and compliance with the Basel Core Principles, among others.

Asked about the matter, former Bangladesh Bank Chief Economist Mustafa K Mujeri told Prothom Alo, “If we can ensure the proper use of technology, it will be possible to address risks in the banking sector in the future. However, simply purchasing technology will not solve the problems of the banking sector. We must also develop skilled personnel to ensure its effective use.”

The economist also stressed the need to ensure transparency and accountability at every stage, from project planning through to implementation.

item.title: Bangladesh Missions abroad go offline due to technical issues with DIP server
item.description:
The government is working to address the technical issues as soon as possible and help the Bangladesh Missions abroad deal with visa processing issues, as the server is currently unavailable.
“Efforts are underway to address the technical issues as soon as possible,” a senior official told UNB on Monday night, noting that due to technical issues with the central system of the Department of Immigration and Passports (DIP), Bangladesh, the MRV (Machine Readable Visa) server is currently unavailable.
He said all the Missions abroad are facing the same problem. A visa applicant who applied from a European country told UNB that he submitted his visa application online but has been unable to proceed with the process due to the technical issue.
“Although the system indicated that I would receive an email within 24 hours of submitting the application, I have not received any email so far, while repeated calls have gone unanswered,” said the applicant.
Due to the technical issues, the processing of NVR (No Visa Required (NVR)) and visa applications and the issuance of visas at the Bangladesh Missions abroad are experiencing a temporary delay.
The Department of Immigration and Passports (DIP), Bangladesh, is working to resolve the technical issues and restore the central system at the earliest possible time.
The government has requested the applicants to allow additional time for the processing of their applications and to refrain from making repeated enquiries regarding the status of their applications during this period.
Meanwhile, the Embassy of Bangladesh, Berlin, in an urgent notice, regretted any inconvenience caused and appreciated the patience, understanding and cooperation of all concerned.
Applicants will be informed via the websites and Facebook pages of the Missions abroad once the central system is restored and normal visa services resume.
Another official said the Department of Immigration and Passports (DIP) conveyed to the Missions abroad the information regarding the technical issues last week, as it is applicable to all.
The Embassy of Bangladesh in Bangkok, in a public message on Tuesday, said it informed all visa service seekers that, due to a temporary technical issue with the visa server, applicants may experience difficulties in submitting visa applications and/or receiving visa-related services.
The embassy said the concerned technical team is working to resolve the issue as soon as possible.
Applicants have been requested to bear with the temporary inconvenience and, where possible, avoid making urgent travel arrangements dependent on immediate visa processing until the system is fully restored.
The embassy regretted the inconvenience caused and appreciated the patience and understanding of all concerned.
